Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Barfoot
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/21/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 232 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of the Board of Pardons and Paroles (Board), by an undetermined amount, depending on the number of Class A and Class B violent offenders assigned by a judge to a parole officer of the Board, as a condition of bond, pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary

Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Barfoot
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/01/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 232 as passed the Senate would increase the administrative obligations of the Board of Pardons and Paroles (Board), by an undetermined amount, depending on the number of defendants charged with Class A or Class B violent felony offenses ordered by a judge to supervision by the Board, as a condition of bond, pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund
